Revised assessment: The statement signals a solid macro backdrop—“strong” activity, robust job gains, low unemployment, and inflation near 2%—paired with a 25 bp hike and ongoing balance‑sheet runoff. The emphasis on “further gradual increases” aligns with rule-like policy responses to activity and inflation (Taylor-style guidance; see Lubik & Schorfheide 2004) and with sticky-information expectations that justify gradualism to anchor inflation (Mankiw & Reis 2002). The symmetric 2% objective and “little changed” long-run expectations, together with real-time output-gap uncertainty (Orphanides 2001), temper exuberance. Labor-market frictions imply inflation pressures can emerge only gradually from tight labor markets (Blanchard & Galí 2008; Ravenna & Walsh 2008). Overall tone: moderately positive but measured.
